title: Leonard Parker's playing style
summary: Foster describes Parker as a smooth, fast, all-round trumpeter who played from his own ideas, like Cottrell, and who died about six years earlier.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Did he read much, do you know, or was it all a head...
He read, but he had a lot of stuff. His own ideas. He had lots of... He had a lot of his own ideas.
What was his tone like? Was he sort of rough or was he fast?
He was a fast man. He was smooth and fast. That's right. He was what you would say an artist on a planet. That's right. He was an old place. You didn't know him.
Is anybody around here sounding like him? I've heard of him, but I don't remember listening at him playing.
Did he sound like, say, George Lewis or Louis Cottrell or...
You might as well say Contreras.
More like Cottrell. Yeah, it was something like that. But he was all around. He was Dixieland. He played sweet, hot. He was on, you know...
On ideas. And play what you put in front of him. So he was a great clan. He didn't know him. He's dead now, but that's what he was.
You know when he died about?
He's dead now about... Oh, I would say at least about... Easy, I'd say. About six years.
